sections.description:
• 1.7 𝙆𝘽 𝙨𝙘𝙧𝙞𝙥𝙩: 𝗅𝗈𝖺𝖽𝖾𝖽 𝖺𝗌𝗒𝗇𝖼 · 𝗇𝗈 𝗂𝗆𝗉𝖺𝖼𝗍 𝗈𝗇 𝗌𝗉𝖾𝖾𝖽
  • 𝙏𝙚𝙨𝙩𝙚𝙙: 𝗈𝗇 𝖺 𝗌𝗂𝗍𝖾 𝗐𝗂𝗍𝗁 250,000 𝗏𝗂𝗌𝗂𝗍𝗌/𝖽𝖺𝗒
  • 𝙍𝙚𝙖𝙡 𝙩𝙞𝙢𝙚: who is on your site
.--------------.------------.------------------------------------.
| OG Analytics | Others     | Feature                            |
:--------------+------------+------------------------------------:
| ~2 ms        | 200–600 ms | Server time per visit              |
| ✓            | ✗          | Zero external requests             |
| ✓            | ✗          | No WP-Cron (stats never get stuck) |
| ✓            | paid/~     | Visitors online now, live          |
| 1.7 KB       | 3–28 KB    | Tracking script (gzip)             |
| ✓            | ~          | Works with any cache plugin & SPA  |
'--------------'------------'------------------------------------'

Real-time analytics inside WordPress: visitors online now, page views, unique and returning visitors, traffic sources and channels, countries and cities on a world map, devices and browsers, time on site, bounce rate, entry pages, 404 pages, site search, “Views” column for posts and pages, bot and referrer spam filtering, CSV export, no cookies and much more…
sections.faq:
Does it use any external service?

Only to show countries and cities: it downloads the free IP to City Lite database by DB-IP (https://db-ip.com) once after activation and then monthly, and reads it on your own server, so no IP address is sent anywhere. License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) — IP Geolocation by DB-IP. Terms and privacy: https://db-ip.com/legal

To show the icon of the websites that send you visitors, once a day (at your site’s quietest hour) it downloads the favicon of up to 100 of those websites directly from each one, and keeps it on your own server. Only the website’s address is used: nothing about your visitors is sent. Well-known sources (Google, Facebook, ChatGPT…) use icons included in the plugin. To turn it off, add add_filter( 'onlygrow_analytics_fetch_favicons', '__return_false' ); to your theme’s functions.php.

Can I keep the statistics of the plugin I used before?

Yes. Tools → Import history finds the data of WP Statistics, Independent Analytics, Burst Statistics, Koko Analytics, Statify, SlimStat, Matomo, Visitor Traffic, WP Visitor Statistics or Post Views Counter on your site and brings in the days before OG Analytics started counting: daily page views, visits, pages, sources, devices and countries. Their data is only read, never changed, and the import can be undone.

Does it work with caching and optimization plugins?

Yes, with nothing to set up. Visits are recorded by the browser, so cached pages count too, and the tracking script protects itself from being combined or delayed until a click. Tested one by one with their most aggressive options (page cache, combine, defer and delay JavaScript): LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, WP Fastest Cache, WP-Optimize, WP Rocket, Jetpack Boost, Speed Optimizer (SiteGround), Breeze, Hummingbird, Cache Enabler, Super Page Cache, Powered Cache, Comet Cache, Autoptimize, Async JavaScript and Flying Scripts. If visits stop arriving, Tools → Diagnose tells you why.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

It stays, so it comes back if you reinstall. To remove everything, turn on “Delete all data when the plugin is uninstalled” in Settings → Data.
sections.changelog:
0.2.19

  • [[improved]] The admin screens have been redesigned to keep improving your experience. In Settings → Design, Settings → Track, Settings → Exclusions, Settings → Data and Settings → WP admin, each group of options now sits in its own card with one line on what it does. The switches sit to the left of their text (as in WordPress), and the lists of roles and content types are plain checkboxes.
  • [[improved]] Settings → Exclusions → IP addresses: add them one by one, or paste a whole list at once.
  • [[new]] In a visitor’s journey, a visit that bounced but ended in a conversion recorded by OG Connectors is marked “Bounce for OG Analytics”, with a note that the conversion still counts there.
  • [[changed]] Deleting the data of some IP addresses and resetting the statistics moved from Settings → Data to their own screen, Tools → Delete data. “Delete this visitor’s data”, in a visitor’s details, still takes you there with their addresses filled in.
  • [[changed]] Tools → Export: exporting and importing your settings now sit side by side, and Tools → Import history shows a placeholder while it looks for other statistics plugins.
  • [[changed]] The plugin is called OG Analytics in its own screens too (the menu, the page title and the welcome steps).

0.2.18

  • [[feature]] OG Analytics and OG Connectors now work together: each lead, form, sign-up or click that OG Connectors records is tied to the visit and the source that brought the visitor, with no cookies, so it works even when the cookie banner is declined. Those conversions also appear in the visitor’s journey, in the visit where they happened. Free in both plugins.
  • [[new]] In the welcome steps (and once after this update), you can choose to help improve the OnlyGrow plugins. Your answer applies to every OnlyGrow plugin on the site, and “Not now” is always an option.
  • [[improved]] Settings → Data: deleting a visitor’s data by IP now also deletes what OG Connectors recorded for that visitor.
  • [[changed]] A cleaner look that feels part of WordPress: the WordPress admin font instead of a monospaced one, the same gray lines and black as the WordPress menu, and white cards. The plugin is also lighter: it no longer ships its own font files.
  • [[compatibility]] SiteGround Speed Optimizer with WooCommerce: “Combine JavaScript” no longer stops visits from being counted.

0.2.17

  • [[new]] After your first week, a short note inviting you to rate the plugin on WordPress.org; after two weeks, where to ask if you have any questions. Each one shows once and goes away for good when you close it.
  • [[new]] Security scanners that probe your site are now recognized as bots: a visit whose address carries an injection attempt (a search for {{7*7}}, a script tag, an SQL trick or a path to system files) is kept apart from your real visitors.
  • [[improved]] Much less database work on busy sites: time on page, who is online and closed tabs are now saved in batches. With 200 visitors at the same time, a minute of activity went from about 3,600 database queries to 5, and it no longer falls behind.
  • [[improved]] A report that would take too long now stops after 20 seconds and tells you to try a shorter date range or fewer filters, instead of keeping your database busy after the page has given up. Counting your visits in the background is never cut short.
  • [[changed]] Reports → Geo is now called Reports → Geolocation.
  • [[security]] The address that receives your visits now accepts at most 16 KB per request (a normal visit is about 2 KB), and the extra data of a custom event is limited to 4 KB, so nobody can fill your site with oversized records.
  • [[fixed]] In the welcome steps, a quick double click on “Next” skipped a step.

0.2.16

  • [[feature]] Tools → Import history: bring your statistics from WP Statistics, Independent Analytics, Burst Statistics, Koko Analytics, Statify, SlimStat, Matomo, Visitor Traffic, WP Visitor Statistics or Post Views Counter. The plugin finds their data on its own; the days before OG Analytics started counting come in day by day (page views, visits, pages, sources, devices and countries), nothing is counted twice, and you can undo it.
  • [[new]] A short welcome the first time you open OG Analytics after installing it: three steps on the visits Google Analytics never sees, why your site stays fast and your data stays yours, and, if you used another statistics plugin, how to bring its history in one click.
  • [[compatibility]] Tested one by one with 17 caching and optimization plugins, each with its most aggressive options (page cache, combine, defer and delay JavaScript): LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, WP Fastest Cache, WP-Optimize, WP Rocket, Jetpack Boost, Speed Optimizer, Breeze, Hummingbird, Cache Enabler, Super Page Cache, Powered Cache, Comet Cache, Autoptimize, Async JavaScript and Flying Scripts. Visits count with all of them, with nothing to exclude by hand.
  • [[improved]] When the address of the tracking script changes (turning ghost mode on or off in Settings → Track), the cache of your caching plugin is cleared on its own, so cached pages switch to the new address right away (WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, WP Fastest Cache, WP-Optimize, Jetpack Boost, Speed Optimizer, Breeze, Hummingbird, Cache Enabler, Super Page Cache, Powered Cache, Comet Cache, Autoptimize).
  • [[fixed]] With WP-Optimize (combine and delay JavaScript), visitors who did not touch the page were not counted.
  • [[fixed]] With Powered Cache (combine and delay JavaScript, or its minifier without its .htaccess rules), visits were not counted.

0.2.15

  • [[improved]] Settings → Data → “Delete all data when the plugin is uninstalled”: if no other OnlyGrow plugin is left on the site, nothing at all is left behind (the shared tables and the site type go too).

0.2.14

  • [[fixed]] A new install was recorded as if it came from an older version, so a future notice meant only for those who updated could have shown to it (installs of 0.2.13 are corrected on their own).

0.2.13

  • [[new]] Notices at the top of the plugin screens, with the look of WordPress: important news is shown once to each administrator, and a closed notice stays closed.
  • [[new]] If the country database has not been downloaded yet, a notice says so and offers “Download now” (it downloads in the background: you can keep working or leave the page) and tells you when it is ready.
  • [[improved]] The “Visitors online now” table on the Dashboard shows everyone who is online, 15 per page (before, only the last 10).
  • [[improved]] After an update, the database changes of the new version are applied right away, without waiting for the next visit.
  • [[improved]] Settings → Data → “Delete all data when the plugin is uninstalled” also removes what each user’s notices saved.
  • [[changed]] New menu icon: the wolf shield of the OnlyGrow family.
  • [[fixed]] If the hosting stopped the download of the country database halfway, it was retried every few minutes (now it waits a few hours).

0.2.12

  • [[new]] Settings → Exclusions: a daily limit of page views per visitor (300 by default). Whoever goes over it is a bot, and that whole day is left out of your numbers.
  • [[new]] Bots disguised as a normal browser are recognized by how their browser behaves (no screen, no languages, a fake Chrome…).
  • [[improved]] More bots recognized, including the ones that do not call themselves “bot” (GoogleOther, Google’s inspection tool, AI assistants, uptime monitors, security scanners).
  • [[improved]] Time on page counts only while someone is there: a tab left open with no activity stops adding time after 30 minutes, and coming back later starts a new visit.
  • [[improved]] More accurate countries: addresses sent with a port are understood, Cloudflare’s country is used when the location database does not know the address, and saved locations are refreshed with each new database.
  • [[improved]] Locations that no visit uses anymore are removed in the daily cleanup.
  • [[fixed]] Visitors on CUBOT phones were counted as bots.
  • [[fixed]] Right after an update, the first screen of the plugin could show “Route not found”.
  • [[fixed]] Form messages (a required field, “Drag to reorder”…) now follow your site’s language.

0.2.10

  • [[new]] The classic editor shows the chart of each post too, in a box on the side.
  • [[new]] Reports → Times: download each chart as CSV (by hour, by day of the week and the day × hour grid).
  • [[improved]] Works with WP Rocket and Autoptimize without excluding anything by hand: the tracking script is left as it is.
  • [[improved]] Clearer “View details” window: menu paths and notes are easier to read.
  • [[changed]] Pause tracking moved to Settings → Track.
  • [[changed]] The dashboard widget shows only visits, and a new icon for Tools.
  • [[fixed]] With WP Rocket’s “Delay JavaScript execution”, visitors who did not touch the page were not counted.
  • [[fixed]] After an update, the plugin screens could keep old styles until the browser cache was cleared.
  • [[fixed]] Tools → Diagnose no longer warns when an optimization plugin serves its own copy of the tracking script.
  • [[fixed]] The table in Tools → Diagnose no longer overflows its card.

0.2.09

  • [[new]] Paid AI channel: visits from ads inside ChatGPT are recognized.
  • [[new]] Websites that send you visitors show their own icon, downloaded once a day at your site’s quietest hour.
  • [[new]] Tools → Export with the same filters as the reports.
  • [[new]] Tools → Export: hourly totals.
  • [[improved]] Tools → Diagnose warns when a cache serves your pages with an old address of the tracker.
  • [[improved]] Smaller, lighter changelog labels.
  • [[fixed]] Ad clicks that arrive without a referrer (Google Ads on iPhone, Microsoft Ads, TikTok, LinkedIn…) were counted as Direct.
  • [[fixed]] Each ad click no longer shows up as a separate page.
  • [[fixed]] Cached pages keep counting after you turn ghost mode on or off.
  • [[fixed]] Reports work on hosts that limit large database queries.
  • [[fixed]] The “Every visit” export uses your site’s time zone.
  • [[changed]] Visit details are kept for 18 months; daily totals are kept forever.

0.2.08

  • [[new]] Every report has its own layout: Visitors, Geo, Devices, Pages, Entry pages and Sources.
  • [[new]] Content report: views by category, tag, your own taxonomies and author. Click a row to filter the whole report.
  • [[new]] Times report: when your visitors arrive, by hour, by day of the week and on a day × hour grid.
  • [[new]] Visitor journey: click the time of any visit to see that visitor’s visits and pages, in order.
  • [[new]] Download any table as CSV, choosing the columns, and print any report to PDF.
  • [[new]] Growth per row: how much each page, source or country grew against the previous period.
  • [[new]] New filters: site search (what people searched on your site) and continent.
  • [[new]] From Content, see the visits of a category, tag or author in one click.
  • [[new]] Tools → Diagnose: everything that can stop your site from counting, with what to do and a report to copy for support.
  • [[new]] A notice on the Dashboard when visits stop arriving at an hour that usually has them.
  • [[new]] A log of the page views your exclusion rules discarded, by reason.
  • [[new]] Tools → Export / Import your settings, and Tools → Restore defaults.
  • [[new]] Pause tracking without deactivating the plugin, with a notice on the Dashboard.
  • [[new]] Visits from comment spammers are not counted (spam comments and Disallowed Comment Keys).
  • [[new]] The views counter can wait until a post reaches a number of views.
  • [[new]] Dashboard widget: a comparison with the previous period (today, yesterday, 7 and 30 days, 12 months).
  • [[improved]] Changelog labels with a cleaner outline style.
  • [[improved]] On wide screens, the Dashboard shows four cards next to the chart.
  • [[improved]] Unique visitors per month and the sources of each entry page are kept forever.
  • [[improved]] More bots detected: user agents that include a web address or an email.
  • [[security]] A visitor’s IP address can no longer be faked with a header. Cloudflare and server proxies are detected on their own.
  • [[fixed]] Tracking works with Cloudflare Rocket Loader.
  • [[fixed]] No more false “REST API blocked” notice when your login session expires.
  • [[changed]] Visit details are kept for 12 months; daily totals are kept forever.
  • [[changed]] A new menu icon.

0.2.07

  • [[changed]] Changelog with color labels.

0.2.06

  • New changelog styles.

0.2.05

  • Sort the Visitors, Pages and Entry pages tables by any number column.
  • Key numbers show the change against the previous period (↗ / ↘), with the details on hover.
  • Counts page changes on single-page apps (sites that switch pages without reloading).

0.2.04

  • Visitors online now, under the main chart: where they come from, the page they are on and their time on site, live.
  • A one-time question about your kind of site, to set up the plugin for you.

0.2.03

  • A simpler, cleaner dashboard and reports.

0.2.02

  • New dashboard: visits chart, key numbers, visitors online, and top pages, sources, devices and countries with a world map.
  • New reports: Visitors, Pages and Entry pages.
  • Inside WordPress: views in the admin bar, a chart in the block editor sidebar and on the WordPress dashboard.
  • Referrer spam and known bots are kept out of your numbers.
  • Ghost mode (on by default): the script and the address that receives visits use a neutral name, so ad blockers don’t stop them.
  • IP addresses are now anonymized by default. Addresses stored before are anonymized once, in the background (this cannot be undone).
  • New “AI Assistants” channel: visits from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Copilot and others no longer count as Referral.
  • iPads and Android tablets are now counted as tablets (before: desktop and mobile).
  • The real screen size and pixel density of each device are recorded.
  • Campaigns (UTM) are kept forever, by source, medium, campaign, term and content.
  • A session is shared by all the tabs of the same browser.
  • A bounce is now a single-page visit of less than 10 seconds with no interaction.
  • Visits by logged-in users record which user it was.

0.2.01

  • New analytics engine: sessions, visitors, sources, campaigns, devices, events, bounce rate, daily totals and retention.
  • Events are queued and processed in batches.

short_description: See every visit the second it happens — fast even with millions of views, and stored only in your own database.
